description: Now that the MAF path is proven end-to-end (FEAT-004), delete the replaced custom-format code, remove Scriban, add the architecture-test seam rule, port the remaining tests to the new boundary, and update the spec/docs (design sections 13, 15, 18, FR-20). This feature leaves the full solution green with no references to deleted types. Depends on FEAT-004 (and all prior). This is the last feature; after it, the whole suite must pass.
steps: Architecture test (design section 13): in backend/tests/Flowgent.Architecture.Tests (DependencyRulesTests) add a rule that no type outside the Flowgent.Runtime.Maf namespace may depend on the Microsoft.Agents.AI.Workflows.Declarative assembly/namespaces, and confirm Definitions does not reference the declarative package and the no-AspNetCore rules still hold. Run it BEFORE the deletions so the seam isolation is validated against the FEAT-003 code.

Delete custom-format code (design section 15 Delete list): remove backend/src/Engine/Flowgent.Definitions/Validation/DefinitionValidator.cs; backend/src/Engine/Flowgent.Definitions/Expressions/TemplateEngine.cs + ScriptConversion.cs; backend/src/Engine/Flowgent.Definitions/Model/WorkflowDefinition.cs (incl. RuleDefinition/RuleStep/MapStep/etc.); backend/src/Engine/Flowgent.Runtime/Execution/WorkflowCompiler.cs (StepExecutor/TerminalStepExecutor); and backend/src/Engine/Flowgent.Runtime/Steps/* EXCEPT the three pieces moved in FEAT-001 (ModuleToolInvoker, StepSchemas, RuleMatcher+MatchRule now live under Modules/ and Matching/). Delete the shims added in FEAT-001 to keep Steps/* compiling. Keep backend/src/Engine/Flowgent.Definitions/Yaml/YamlJsonReader.cs.

Schemas (design section 15): remove the workflow-format entry from backend/src/Engine/Flowgent.Definitions/Schemas/FormatSchemas.cs and delete backend/schemas/workflow.schema.json; keep module.schema.json + samples.schema.json. Drop the 'workflow' name from the /api/engine/schemas/{name} endpoint (documented behavior change) and update any test listing schema names.
Scriban (design section 15): remove the Scriban PackageReference/version from backend/Directory.Packages.props (and any csproj that referenced it) once nothing references it.

Port tests (design section 18, 4.3): rewrite tests that asserted deleted step-format validator messages (e.g. 'unknown step kind', 'unreachable step', Scriban template load errors) to assert the declarative builder's error for an equivalent malformed declarative document (via the trial-build validator), or remove them with the behavior change documented in the PR. Port invalid-module tests to the new boundary (bad agent/tool/sample reference or missing schema file still reported via envelope checks; a malformed declarative workflow reported via the trial build). Enumerate the existing DefinitionValidator-touching tests so none is silently dropped (AC-16). Ensure backend/tests/Flowgent.Integration.Tests still cover the two Demo end-to-end flows, HITL resume, the MCP bridge, the gRPC-Web path via the gateway, and the Global.<stepId> snapshot read.

Docs/spec (FR-20): mark the Phase 2 items done in .kiro/specs/maf-declarative-migration/tasks.md and update docs/* pages that describe the custom YAML format / Scriban / step kinds to the MAF declarative + PowerFx model (platform docs use generic/template examples; module docs stay in the module folders).
Final full build + test and confirm no reference to any deleted type remains.

HANDOFF FROM FEAT-004: migrate the test-only fixtures module (backend/tests/Fixtures/Flowgent.Fixtures.Module) to MAF declarative. It was deferred (Option B) because it is already RED since FEAT-003 (old custom format is invalid under the new loader, not a FEAT-004 regression) and its integration-test porting is this feature's task 2.6. Migrate both fixture YAMLs (fixture-flow, fixture-rules) + manifest to the descriptor form, remove demo: blocks, and add the (fixture-flow, draft) Demo key to DemoResponseProvider.

HANDOFF FROM FEAT-004 (the http step): the `http` step kind is the ONE kind NOT yet exercised on MAF; FEAT-004 proved llm/map/rule/tool/human-input/terminal but not http. Do NOT silently ship an unverified declarative HTTP action. Either (a) PROBE the declarative HTTP action in spike/Spike.MafDeclarative first and use it if faithful, OR (b) bridge the fixture echo through a new fixture.echo module tool (a fixture-service change) via InvokeMcpTool — but make that an EXPLICIT documented choice. If you bridge via a tool, record that a genuine declarative HTTP action remains UNPROVEN as a known gap, since real modules may later need an http step.

HANDOFF FROM FEAT-004 (two integration-test changes, SAME documented observability-contract-change classes already approved for support): (1) FixtureModuleTests.Definition_IsValidAndCoversEveryStepKind asserts the OLD 'kind: http/llm/map/rule/tool/human-input/terminal' strings appear in the YAML text — incompatible with declarative (InvokeAzureAgent/InvokeMcpTool/Question/ConditionGroup/SendActivity); re-express it against the declarative action kinds + the manifest terminal outcomes. (2) FixtureModuleTests.Rules_SeveralMatches_FailWithTheDeclaredMessage expects CurrentStepId=='classify' on an ambiguous-rule failure — under MAF a rule failure is a GotoAction to an explicit failure terminal, so CurrentStepId is that terminal (same Gap-3 change as support's RoutingFailures). Update both with inline findings-references to FEAT-004-observability-gap-analysis.md; preserve business outcomes (Completed/Failed, verbatim messages, group/queue/runHeader outputs).

HANDOFF FROM FEAT-004 (baseline failures): keep the pre-existing baseline-failure list distinct from the deferred-RED set. Tasks.md records 7 pre-existing Flowgent.Engine.Tests failures on commit 95a4aea (module-loader YAML-text-patch fixtures, unrelated to this migration). FEAT-005 must clear the deferred-RED set (fixtures + integration + ported engine tests) AND ideally the 7-8 pre-existing ones, or explicitly document any that stay out of scope.
acceptance_criteria: DependencyRulesTests includes the seam-isolation rule and all existing architecture rules pass.

DefinitionValidator, TemplateEngine, ScriptConversion, WorkflowDefinition, WorkflowCompiler, the custom Steps/* handlers, and backend/schemas/workflow.schema.json are deleted; Scriban is removed from central package management; YamlJsonReader is retained.
The /api/engine/schemas/{name} endpoint no longer lists 'workflow'; affected tests updated.
`dotnet build backend/Flowgent.slnx` succeeds and `dotnet test --solution backend/Flowgent.slnx` passes with the full suite green (engine, integration, architecture, gateway, module tests).
.kiro/specs/maf-declarative-migration/tasks.md Phase 2 boxes are checked and docs/* reflect the MAF declarative model.
findings:
DONE + verified. `dotnet build backend/Flowgent.slnx` 0 warnings/0 errors; `dotnet test --solution backend/Flowgent.slnx` 278/278 green (engine, integration, architecture, gateway, support, template); `dotnet test --project backend/tests/Flowgent.Architecture.Tests` 27/27.

ARCHITECTURE SEAM RULE (step 1): added DependencyRulesTests.OnlyTheMafSeam_ReferencesTheDeclarativePackage (no type outside Flowgent.Runtime.Maf depends on Microsoft.Agents.AI.Workflows.Declarative) + Definitions_DoesNotReferenceTheDeclarativePackage. Both run and passed BEFORE the deletions against the FEAT-003 seam code (validated isolation), and still pass after.

DELETIONS (steps 2-4): removed DefinitionValidator.cs, Expressions/{TemplateEngine,ScriptConversion}.cs, Model/WorkflowDefinition.cs, Execution/WorkflowCompiler.cs, Steps/* (StepHandlers, LlmStepHandler, HumanInputAndHttpHandlers) — kept the FEAT-001 relocations Modules/ModuleToolInvoker.cs, Modules/StepSchemas.cs, Matching/RuleMatcher.cs(+MatchRule). Removed the orphan WorkflowDocument shim and the transitional RunContext members (Templates/CreateScope/CreateIntakeScope/StepMessage); kept EnterStep/CurrentStepId (used by the MAF orchestrator). FormatSchemas lost the workflow entry; backend/schemas/workflow.schema.json deleted (module.schema.json + samples.schema.json kept). /api/engine/schemas/{name} serves only module+samples (documented behavior change). Scriban removed from backend/Directory.Packages.props + Flowgent.Definitions.csproj; YamlDotNet kept. Confirmed no source reference to any deleted type remains.

HTTP STEP DECISION (handoff): chose OPTION B (bridge) — the fixture echo 'external API' is reached as a new fixture.echo module tool via InvokeMcpTool/ModuleToolHandler (runHeader = ToolInvocation.RunId, matching the old X-Fixture-Run header). A GENUINE DECLARATIVE HTTP ACTION REMAINS UNPROVEN — KNOWN GAP: real modules that need an http step are not yet covered; a future spike must prove the declarative HTTP action before shipping one.

FIXTURES MIGRATION (handoff): migrated backend/tests/Fixtures to MAF declarative (fixture-flow: draft agent / shape map / reverse+echo tools / review Question+ConditionGroup / done|declined terminals; fixture-rules: classify ConditionGroup rule / routed|ambiguous). Added DemoResponseProvider keys (fixture-flow,draft), (hello,summarize), (review,write). Added EchoTool to the fixture service + fixture.echo to the manifest.

SEAM FIX (generic, needed for module-down): MafRunDriver.DescribeError now prefers the innermost StepFailedException message (and ExecutorFailedEvent uses it too), so a module-tool failure surfaces its descriptive reason ('Module \u0027...\u0027 is unavailable...') instead of the declarative builder's generic 'Unhandled workflow failure - #echo (InvokeMcpTool)'.

TEST PORTING: ModuleLoaderTests re-expressed against the envelope (manifest/sample/schema-file checks) + trial-build boundary; the deleted custom step-graph validator checks (unknown step kind, unreachable/no-terminal, template/condition/regex, duplicate step ids, terminal-with-next, maxSteps, Scriban assignAgent, per-step demo: block, rule onMultipleMatches/onNoMatch policies, map lookups) were removed as documented behavior changes. ScriptConversionProperties.cs + TemplateEngineTests.cs deleted (tested the deleted Scriban engine, no C# equivalent). TestModules hello/review workflows rewritten to declarative. A malformed declarative workflow is now reproduced by a GotoAction to a non-existent action id (the declarative builder is lenient about unknown trigger/action kinds and a missing trigger, so those do NOT fail the trial build).

DOCUMENTED OBSERVABILITY/BEHAVIOR CONTRACT CHANGES encoded in ported tests (business outcomes preserved): (1) routing/rule failures end at the explicit failure TERMINAL id, so run.CurrentStepId is the terminal (fail_ambiguous/fail_no_app/fail_no_team/ambiguous), not the rule step — same Gap-3 class as support RoutingFailures; (2) a module tool's ToolInvocationRequest.StepId carries the tool name (InvokeMcpTool does not surface the logical step id to the seam) while run.CurrentStepId still resolves to the step; (3) an agent step sends only the authored user prompt — no per-step systemPrompt/temperature/output-schema on the call (LLM output is validated downstream, so a malformed/fenced response fails the run at the parse, and the provider error surfaces raw, not wrapped as 'LLM call failed for step ...'); (4) /api/engine/schemas drops 'workflow'; (5) the dashboard graph shows the snapshot steps + manifest terminals, without branch-condition edge labels; (6) ModuleDownTests in-flight tool failure can land on reverse or echo (both are module tools now) — a timing detail, so the test asserts either with the descriptive message.

TEST-INFRA (load, NOT logic): the heavyweight in-process test assemblies (Flowgent.Integration.Tests, Flowgent.Engine.Tests) now run serially (xunit.runner.json parallelizeTestCollections=false) and the PlatformHarness/TestEngine/EngineTestHost HITL/terminal waits were widened (15s/10s -> 60s) because the MAF per-run JSON checkpoint I/O is heavier than the old engine; under the full `dotnet test --solution` load (6 assemblies in parallel) the bounded waits flaked otherwise. ConcurrentRuns_AreIsolated reduced 20->6 runs; ModuleDownTests draft demo latency raised 1500ms->8000ms for a reliable stop window; SequentialProcessing_StartsOneRunAtATime dispatch-loops until the second run leaves the queue.

DOCS/SPEC (FR-20): tasks.md Phase 2 boxes 2.5/2.6 checked. docs/workflow-reference.md and docs/expressions.md rewritten to the MAF declarative + PowerFx model (built-in flowgent.input/parse, Global.<stepId> snapshots, reserved terminal globals, ConditionGroup/GotoAction routing, Lower+Find instead of IsMatch, trial-build validation). docs/demo-mode.md (DemoResponseProvider keyed by workflow/step, no demo: block), docs/human-input.md (Question+ConditionGroup + flowgent.parse resume), docs/architecture.md (MafWorkflowFactory/MafRunDriver instead of WorkflowCompiler; PowerFx instead of Scriban; no maxSteps), docs/debugging.md (new 'No demo response is defined' message) updated.

BASELINE-FAILURE NOTE: the handoff mentioned '7 pre-existing Flowgent.Engine.Tests failures'; in reality the entire Engine.Tests suite (95 failures) was built on the deleted custom format + custom-format TestModules/TestEngine helpers, so it was ported wholesale here (not 7). After porting, Engine.Tests is 133/133 and the full solution is 278/278 — nothing left out of scope.

Phase 2.7 (readability cleanup, R8) is a separate non-blocking housekeeping item and was left unchecked (out of this FEAT's scope).
